summary: Cohort Studio implements the distinct Studio workflow: editable operations, counts of rows versus samples versus patients, inflation-aware fixes, unique cohort IDs and a standalone reconstruction script. The most important concerns are an unknown-checksum state being described as verified, unsafe interpolation of request text into generated Python, and reconstruction continuing after input-hash mismatch. The final concern is an explicit trust-policy question, not a claim that Studio must obey every Control Tower contract.
limitations: Pinned local checkout, not a verified official final-submission receipt; branch names and later changes are outside this pass.
Static source analysis only. No submission code, tests, installers, workflows, notebook, server, hosted endpoint or model was executed.
No sealed envelopes, answer keys or raw clinical datasets were accessed. Numerical correctness, performance, accessibility and fresh-machine setup remain untested.
Source-derived control-flow consequences are labeled as such. Proposed acceptance checks are not observed test results.
The collected text budget is 160 files, 200 KB/file and 4 MB/entry. Complete_with_exclusions is not an exhaustive audit; exclusions and focused follow-ups are recorded.
No official score, cross-team ranking, clinical validity or regulatory/accessibility certification is asserted.

criteria.assessment: Step counts and join-inflation evidence fit the Studio product. Detection accuracy and real-cohort inclusion were not independently measured.

findings.title: Step ledgers distinguish rows, samples and patients
findings.observation: Each applied step records incoming and outgoing row, distinct-sample and distinct-patient counts. The engine identifies growth in rows per sample, records duplicate counts and examples, and the verdict distinguishes unresolved inflation from inflation later resolved by a step or logged fix.
findings.impact: This directly addresses a central Studio failure mode: join multiplicity can increase rows without adding independent samples or patients. The source makes the distinction inspectable instead of presenting one misleading cohort size.
findings.recommendation: Retain all three count dimensions and the exact join rule. Explain intentional one-to-many data separately from accidental inflation and keep counts before and after any fix visible.
findings.acceptance_check: Join one invented sample to two slide records. Verify rows increase, distinct samples do not, the ledger names the inflating step, and a later exists-style fix retains the intended sample exactly once.
findings.confidence: High for the inspected count and inflation construction; no join fixture was run in this pass.

def run(spec, store):
    problems = validate(spec, store)
    frame = store.manifest.copy()
    start_ids = list(frame["sample_id"].unique())
    filtered_vars = set()
    all_links = {}
    results = []
    failed = False
    for i, step in enumerate(spec.get("steps", [])):
        r = StepResult(index=i, label=describe_step(step, store), op=step.get("op", "?"))
        r.rows_in, r.samples_in, r.patients_in = len(frame), frame["sample_id"].nunique(), frame["patient_id"].nunique()
        step_problems = [m for (j, m) in problems if j == i]
        if failed or step_problems:
            r.skipped = True
            r.error = "; ".join(step_problems) if step_problems else "Not run because an earlier step failed."
            failed = True
            results.append(r)
            continue
        try:
            new = apply_step(frame, step, store)
        except Exception as exc:  # show the error in the ledger instead of crashing the app
            r.error, r.skipped, failed = str(exc), True, True
            results.append(r)
            continue
        r.rows_out, r.samples_out, r.patients_out = len(new), new["sample_id"].nunique(), new["patient_id"].nunique()

ratio_in = r.rows_in / r.samples_in if r.samples_in else 1
        if r.samples_out and r.rows_per_sample > ratio_in + 1e-9:
            r.inflated = True
            extra = r.rows_out - r.samples_out
            r.inflation_note = (f"Rows grew to {r.rows_out:,} but there are only {r.samples_out:,} distinct samples "
                                f"({r.patients_out:,} patients): {extra:,} extra rows would count samples more than once.")
            r.duplicate_examples = _duplicate_examples(new, step)
            counts = new["sample_id"].value_counts()
            r.duplicate_counts = {sid: int(n) for sid, n in sorted(counts[counts > 1].items())}

# 4. Join inflation

criteria.assessment: Editable steps and copied, logged fixes expose construction logic. Automatic transformation must remain distinct from human approval of the research meaning.

findings.title: Inflation fixes are explicit copied transformations with a log
findings.observation: suggest_fix chooses exists-style matching for slide/normal joins, sample-level keys for patient-key joins, or a deduplication step. apply_fixes clones the specification and records the old step, row/sample/patient counts, examples and proposed fix. The API retains the first result and list of fixes when it reruns a fixed specification.
findings.impact: This makes the before-versus-after transformation inspectable and preserves evidence of why a cohort changed. Automatic API fixing is not equivalent to human approval, even when the change is logged and originals are not edited.
findings.recommendation: Retain copied specifications, first results and fix logs. Show the semantic change and ask for explicit confirmation before representing the fixed cohort as approved for a research use that depends on join meaning.
findings.acceptance_check: Compare fix=False and fix=True on an inflated synthetic join. Confirm the original specification is unchanged, the first result and exact policy change remain available, and the approved versus preview state is explicit.
findings.confidence: High for clone/log and API return structure; researcher acceptance and end-to-end presentation remain untested.

evidence.quote:
def suggest_fix(step):
    """A minimal change that stops a step counting samples twice, with a plain-words reason."""
    fixed = dict(step)
    if step["op"] == "join" and step["table"] in ("slides", "normals"):
        fixed["mode"] = "exists"
        what = "slide" if step["table"] == "slides" else "normal-tissue sample"
        return fixed, f"Keep each sample once if it has at least one matching {what}, instead of one row per {what}."
    if step["op"] == "join" and step.get("key") == "patient_id":
        fixed["key"] = "sample_id"
        return fixed, ("Match each sample to its own record by sample barcode. Joining on the patient barcode "
                       "also matches the patient's other samples (for example a normal-tissue sample).")
    return None, "Add a 'keep one row per sample' step after this one."

criteria.assessment: Exported specifications and input hashes aid provenance, but unknown checksum state must not be called verified.

findings.title: An unknown checksum can be described as a matching checksum
findings.observation: Raw-file status starts verified=None and becomes True or False only when an expected digest exists. available accepts a present file unless verification is explicitly False. The frozen-file verdict looks only for False and otherwise says every raw file used matches sources.csv. A missing expected digest is therefore not distinguished from a verified match in that check.
findings.impact: A hash of current bytes establishes identity of those bytes, not agreement with the organizer's frozen release. The claim can overstate provenance when expected checksum metadata is absent. This does not establish that ordinary bundled metadata is missing.
findings.recommendation: Preserve distinct missing, unverified, mismatched and verified states. Require True for a matching-checksum claim and mark unavailable expected metadata as unknown with a concrete recovery instruction.
findings.acceptance_check: Use a present synthetic raw file with no expected digest, then a matching digest and a mismatched digest. Only the matching case may claim verification; the unknown case must name the missing reference metadata.
findings.confidence: High for the tri-state control flow; the parallel TESTS.md reports a matching helper-level unknown-to-pass reproduction.

criteria.assessment: Generated-script text boundaries need fixing. Hosted drafting is disclosed in the repository and was not called; no undisclosed transmission or actual leak is claimed.

findings.title: Request text is inserted into a generated Python docstring
findings.observation: reproduce_script places spec.request verbatim between triple-quoted Python docstring delimiters. Most operation arguments later use repr formatting, but this leading prose field is not encoded as a Python literal. Quotes and newlines in request text can therefore break script syntax or terminate the docstring and become code in the exported file.
findings.impact: A reproduction artifact should preserve a user's description as data, not reinterpret it as executable syntax. The dangerous transition occurs if someone later runs the generated script; this review did not execute generated code or establish a deployed attack.
findings.recommendation: Serialize request text safely as a string literal or external JSON metadata and keep executable code structurally separate. Apply the same rule to every user-controlled value and test the resulting artifact without executing arbitrary text.
findings.acceptance_check: Generate scripts from ordinary text, multiline text and text containing triple quotes. Parse the generated syntax in an authorized environment and verify the original request remains a literal value with no extra executable statements.
findings.confidence: High for literal interpolation; the parallel reviewer reports syntax and statement-boundary probes, which were not rerun here.

criteria.assessment: The code exports unique IDs and reconstruction artifacts. The parallel review reports 279 passed and 20 skipped tests; this source pass did not execute them.

findings.title: The export path has unique cohort IDs and inspectable operations
findings.observation: cohort_sample_ids collects IDs into a set and returns them sorted. cohort_frame writes a sample_id column from those IDs. write_all emits the specification, ledger, exclusions, audit trail, sample selections, verdict and reconstruction script alongside cohort_samples.csv. The script serializes most operation arguments with repr.
findings.impact: The artifact set fits the Studio handoff and makes cohort construction more inspectable than a screenshot alone. Unique IDs do not by themselves prove correct inclusion, and the request-docstring issue remains a separate safety defect.
findings.recommendation: Keep the complete export bundle and bind it to a manifest of input and output hashes. Add exact membership parity checks between the app result and an independently reviewed reconstruction.
findings.acceptance_check: For an authorized synthetic specification, compare the app's sorted unique IDs, CSV and reconstructed IDs exactly. Verify the ledger and specification explain each exclusion and that all bundle files share one run identity.
findings.confidence: High for the export construction; fresh-machine reconstruction and output parity were not executed by this reviewer.

evidence.quote:
def write_all(result, verdict, store, out_dir, team="Cohort Studio team"):
    out = pathlib.Path(out_dir)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cohort_frame(result).to_csv(out / "cohort_samples.csv", index=False)
    (out / "cohort_spec.json").write_text(json.dumps(result.spec, indent=2))
    ledger_frame(result).to_csv(out / "ledger.csv", index=False)
    exclusions_frame(result).to_csv(out / "exclusions.csv", index=False)
    audit_trail_frame(result).to_csv(out / "audit_trail.csv", index=False)
    selection_frame(result).to_csv(out / "sample_selection.csv", index=False)
    coverage_frame(result, store).to_csv(out / "coverage.csv", index=False)
    (out / "verdict.json").write_text(json.dumps(verdict.to_dict(), indent=2))
    (out / "reproduce_cohort.py").write_text(reproduce_script(result, store))
    (out / "findings.json").write_text(json.dumps(findings_document(result, verdict, store, team), indent=2))
    return out

criteria.assessment: Before/after fix evidence is useful. Strict reproduction and exploratory reruns should have distinguishable provenance and success criteria.

findings.title: Reconstruction warns about changed inputs but still writes a cohort
findings.observation: The generated script compares current file hashes with EXPECTED and prints a warning when they differ, then continues to load and transform the data. It writes cohort_samples.csv and prints the expected count rather than asserting the original membership. This is an intentional-looking permissive path, not a demonstrated numeric failure.
findings.impact: A usable exploratory rerun on new data is different from a faithful reconstruction of the reviewed cohort. Without a distinct mode or failure state, a reader may mistake a warning-bearing new cohort for a verified reproduction.
findings.recommendation: Decide and document the contract. A strict reproduction mode should stop on hash mismatch and compare membership or an output digest; an exploratory mode can continue but must produce a clearly labeled new run with changed-input provenance.
findings.acceptance_check: Change one synthetic input after export. Confirm strict reconstruction refuses to certify the old cohort, while any permitted exploratory run has a new identity and cannot silently replace the original reproduction result.
findings.confidence: High for the warning-and-continue path; whether strict refusal is required is a product-policy question for judges, not an invented organizer rule.
